strategies.title: [diameter-normalized-active-set] Full constrained diameter polish
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: diameter-normalized-active-set

Replacement scope: Replace the final “recenter and normalize” phase after the incumbent annealing loop with a deterministic SLSQP polish on the best annealed configuration, using translated coordinates with point 0 fixed at the origin.

Compute budget: One SLSQP start, at most 350 iterations, with analytic Jacobians for all 91 lower-distance and 91 upper-diameter constraints; expected added evaluation time is several seconds, not another full annealing run.

Gain mechanism: Parameterize the exact evaluator-visible problem by maximizing an auxiliary variable \(t\) subject to every squared pair distance satisfying \(t\le d_{ij}^2\le1\). After SLSQP, reconstruct the 14 points, reject nonfinite output, compute all 91 actual distances, and retain the polished result only when its exact raw squared ratio exceeds that of the annealed input; otherwise return the annealed input. strategies.plan:

Compute budget: Three deterministic starts, each with at most 180 SLSQP iterations on the five-parameter layered ansatz, followed by at most 25,000 existing annealing iterations after releasing all coordinates; expected total time is below the present eight-by-60,000-proposal budget.

strategies.title: [contact-graph-nullspace] Active-contact nullspace local refinement
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: contact-graph-nullspace

Replacement scope: Replace the final single SLSQP polish block, beginning at “Fix translation and scale” through selection of `polished`, with a two-stage active-contact refinement.

Compute budget: At most 3 deterministic local starts: the incumbent plus two signed perturbations; at most 120 SLSQP iterations per start followed by at most 80 trust-constr iterations on the best SLSQP result. Expected evaluation-time effect: roughly +0.3 to +0.7 seconds, with the annealing budget unchanged.

Gain mechanism: Build an explicit active graph from all pairs with squared distance within 0.4% of the current minimum or maximum squared distance. Compute the Jacobian of these active pair-distance equations after removing translation, rotation, and scale gauge directions. Take the largest right-singular-vector nullspace direction that increases the mean squared length of currently minimum pairs while decreasing the mean squared length of currently maximum pairs. This is a collective contact-preserving motion absent from the incumbent’s one-point annealing proposals and absent from its single direct SLSQP call, which begins from an arbitrary nonsmooth active-set point.

Normalize the incumbent to diameter one and pin point zero at the origin as in the existing code. Form the active lower and upper pair sets using exact all-pairs squared distances. Construct the signed Jacobian: lower-contact rows use positive distance gradients and upper-contact rows use negative distance gradients. Project out coordinate columns corresponding to the gauge-fixed representation, compute an SVD, and use the least-constrained right singular vectors to make two deterministic trial points at signed step sizes chosen by backtracking from `0.003` down to `0.00009375`. Each trial must be rescaled by its actual diameter before entering the constrained solver. Polish all feasible trials with the existing exact inequalities `dij² >= t` and `dij² <= 1`, retaining only an exact all-pairs improvement. Return the original incumbent if all trials fail finite validation.

The result remains a finite `(14, 3)` float array because every candidate is checked for finiteness, recentered, and divided by a strictly positive measured diameter. Expected-gain check: this explicitly tests a collective active-contact nullspace displacement that the incumbent’s final polish does not construct; it is falsified unless the returned exact raw `min_max_ratio` exceeds `0.238909812674` (equivalently combined score exceeds `0.995262387462`).

strategies.title: [seven-vertex-reinsertion] Alternating seven-vertex subsystem reinsertion
strategies.plan:

Freeze one seven-point set and jointly reinsert the other seven points by maximizing an auxiliary lower-bound variable `t`, subject to all pairwise distances between movable points and frozen points, and among movable points, lying in `[t, 1]` after diameter normalization. Then reverse the roles. This provides a mesoscopic seven-point rearrangement and can change several bottleneck contacts simultaneously, unlike the incumbent’s one-point Metropolis move and unlike the prior small local patch replacement.

Finish with the existing full 14-point polish and exact accept-only-if-better comparison.

Optimize center equatorial radius, center axial height, common and axial dimer half-lengths, fivefold ring twist, independent polar tangent azimuths, and a stagger angle coupling the equatorial dimer orientations. This is a distinct contact topology: near contacts can occur both within dimers and between neighboring dimers around the pentagonal belt, while polar dimers create cross-layer contacts unavailable to the two-heptagon construction.

`c[k] = (r cos(2πk/5), r sin(2πk/5), 0)` for `k=0..4`,
`c[5]=(0,0,h)`, and `c[6]=(0,0,-h)`.
For equatorial center `k`, use the unit tangent
`u[k]=cos(beta+2πk/5)(-sin(2πk/5),cos(2πk/5),0)+sin(beta+2πk/5)(0,0,1)`;
for poles use horizontal unit vectors at independent azimuths. Emit `c[i] ± ell[i] u[i]`, normalize by exact diameter, and optimize the stated parameters against the exact squared ratio. Use four deterministic initial parameter vectors spanning short/long dimers and small/large axial height. Pass only the best two exact candidates into the existing unrestricted Cartesian release so symmetry is allowed to break.

All seeds have exactly fourteen finite coordinates; invalid parameter trials are assigned a bad objective, and final output still uses exact measured-diameter normalization. \]

\]

\]
normalized to a common radius. Add six edge points
\[
a(v_i+v_j)+b(v_i-v_j)
\]

strategies.title: [prestress-contact-exchange] Multiplier-guided active-contact swap refinement
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: prestress-contact-exchange

Replacement scope: Replace the final “active contacts with deterministic nullspace-displacement starts” block, from construction of `active` through the SLSQP/trust-constr starts, while retaining the existing dimerized construction, continuation phase, exact `ratio2`, and final normalization.

Compute budget: At most 3 contact-exchange trials; each trial uses one weighted linearized displacement solve and one SLSQP solve of at most 140 iterations. Do not invoke `trust-constr` in this replacement. Expected evaluation-time effect: approximately neutral or modestly lower than the existing SLSQP plus trust-constr block.

Gain mechanism: The incumbent treats all near-minimum and near-diameter contacts equally when forming its nullspace direction. Instead, estimate nonnegative KKT-like multipliers for the current active lower and upper distance constraints by NNLS on their signed coordinate gradients. Retain only contacts with meaningful multiplier, identify lower contacts carrying essentially zero multiplier, and exchange one such geometrically redundant lower contact for the closest inactive pair that is about to become binding. Solve a regularized linear system that increases multiplier-supported lower contacts, contracts multiplier-supported diameter contacts, and keeps the exchanged inactive pair from collapsing. This explicitly changes the local contact topology rather than merely moving in the old active-contact nullspace.

Center and diameter-normalize every generated trial, reject nonfinite trials, and retain the original incumbent whenever no exchanged-contact trial improves the exact all-91-pair ratio. The SLSQP epigraph constraints remain `z_ij >= t` and `z_ij <= 1`, so every returned candidate remains a finite `(14, 3)` array with positive measured diameter after final normalization. Expected-gain check: this is falsifiable by requiring the exchanged-contact candidate to exceed the incumbent raw squared ratio `0.24005088265`; the incumbent’s unweighted single-nullspace displacement cannot deliberately remove a zero-stress contact while promoting a specified imminent inactive contact.

strategies.title: [distance-geometry-patch-completion] Five-vertex Cayley-Menger patch reconstruct
strategies.plan:

Compute budget: Select one five-point patch from each of the two best dimerized candidates. For each patch, enumerate at most 6 boundary-contact patterns and run `least_squares` for at most 90 function evaluations per pattern, followed by one full Cartesian SLSQP of at most 140 iterations for the best reconstructed patch. Expected evaluation-time effect: lower than the current three-start, five-temperature L-BFGS-B continuation, with a bounded additional small least-squares cost.

Gain mechanism: Construct a patch from the five vertices incident to the greatest number of near-minimum contacts, leaving the other nine vertices fixed as anchors. Represent the patch first by its ten internal squared distances and its 45 patch-to-anchor squared distances. For each candidate pattern, impose equal target distance on the patch’s currently shortest internal edges and on its shortest anchor edges, while imposing the observed diameter bound on all patch-to-anchor pairs. Recover coordinates by minimizing the residuals of those squared-distance equations in Cartesian coordinates, with a small displacement penalty from the incumbent patch. This is a distance-geometry completion step: it changes several dependent local distances coherently, unlike the incumbent’s global soft minimum, which can improve one bottleneck while immediately creating another within the same tight local cluster.

Use the all-pairs exact ratio to select among completed patches, then pass only the best finite centered diameter-normalized result to the existing full inequality polish; preserve the untouched incumbent as fallback. Expected-gain check: accept this mechanism only if the reconstructed-and-polished patch reaches raw squared ratio greater than `0.24005088265`, which directly corresponds to combined score greater than `1.00001591355`; it is a falsifiable contact-pattern change unavailable to the incumbent’s fixed smooth continuation.
